item.text: {"case_id":"SHC042","decision":"candidate","candidate_ranking":["C12","C25","C06"],"selected_candidate_label":"C12","confidence":0.99,"relationship_type":"both","rationale":"C12 is the immediately preceding continuation letter for the same Taliban emergency and supplies nearly the entire child’s structure and much of its wording. Both recite section 202(d), report sending the enclosed Federal Register notice, describe Taliban-controlled Afghan territory as a safe haven and base of operations for Usama bin Laden and al-Qaida, characterize the situation as an unusual and extraordinary threat, and conclude that the same emergency authorities must remain in force beyond the anniversary date. The child principally updates the date and makes minor wording and capitalization changes. C25 and C06 share substantial continuation-letter machinery, but neither matches the child’s target and factual paragraph as C12 does.","shared_material":[{"child_excerpt":"Section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1622(d)) provides for the automatic termination of a national emergency unless, prior to the anniversary date of its declaration, the President publishes in the Federal Register and transmits to the Congress a notice","parent_excerpt":"Section 202(d) of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1622(d)) provides for the automatic termination of a national emergency unless, prior to the anniversary date of its declaration, the President publishes in the Federal Register and transmits to the Congress a notice","explanation":"The statutory and procedural opening is identical."},{"child_excerpt":"the emergency declared with respect to the Taliban, is to continue in effect beyond July 4, 2001","parent_excerpt":"the emergency declared with respect to the Taliban is to continue in effect beyond July 5, 2000","explanation":"The same operative sentence is reused with the anniversary date updated."},{"child_excerpt":"The Taliban continues to allow territory under its control in Afghanistan to be used as a safe haven and base of operations for Usama bin Laden and the al-Qaida organization who have committed, and threaten to continue to commit, acts of violence against the United States and its nationals.","parent_excerpt":"The Taliban continues to allow territory under its control in Afghanistan to be used as a safe haven and base of operations for Usama bin Laden and the Al-Qaida organization, who have committed and threaten to continue to commit acts of violence against the United States and its nationals.","explanation":"This distinctive factual justification is nearly verbatim."},{"child_excerpt":"This situation continues to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and foreign policy interests of the United States. For these reasons, I have determined that it is necessary to maintain these emergency authorities in force beyond July 4, 2001.","parent_excerpt":"This situation continues to pose an unusual and extraordinary threat to the national security and foreign policy interests of the United States. For these reasons, I have determined that it is necessary to maintain in force these emergency authorities beyond July 5, 2000.","explanation":"The threat finding and concluding determination are materially identical apart from word order and the updated date."}]}
